Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: chloramphenicol + acetyl-CoA = chloramphenicol 3-acetate + CoA.

Name: choline dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: A + choline = AH(2) + betaine aldehyde.

Name: chorismate lyase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: chorismate = 4-hydroxybenzoate + pyruvate.

Name: citrate CoA-transferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + citrate = acetate + (3S)-citryl-CoA.

Name: citrate (pro-3S)-lyase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: citrate = acetate + oxaloacetate.

Name: citryl-CoA lyase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (3S)-citryl-CoA = acetyl-CoA + oxaloacetate.

Name: corrinoid adenosyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 ATP + 2 corrinoid + reduced [electron-transfer flavoprotein] = 2 adenosylcorrinoid + 3 H+ + oxidized [electron-transfer flavoprotein] + 2 triphosphate. The corrinoid can be cob(II)yrinate a,c diamide, cob(II)inamide or cob(II)alamin.

Name: cobalamin 5'-phosphate synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: adenosylcobinamide-GDP + alpha-ribazole-5'-phosphate = adenosylcobalamin-5'-phosphate + GMP.

Name: cobinamide kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: cobinamide + ATP = cobinamide phosphate + ADP. This reaction is the phosphorylation of the hydroxyl group of the 1-amino-2-propanol residue of cobinamide, in the presence of ATP, to form cobinamide phosphate.

Name: cobinamide phosphate guanylyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: adenosylcobinamide phosphate + GTP + 2 H+ = adenosylcobinamide-GDP + diphosphate.

Name: crossover junction DNA endonuclease activity
Definition: Catalysis of the endonucleolytic cleavage at a junction such as a reciprocal single-stranded crossover between two homologous DNA duplexes (Holliday junction).

Name: obsolete crotonobetaine/carnitine-CoA ligase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: cupric reductase (NADH) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 Cu2+ + NADH = 2 Cu+ + H+ + NAD+.

Name: cyanate hydratase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: cyanate + H2O = carbamate.

Name: cyclopropane-fatty-acyl-phospholipid synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + phospholipid olefinic fatty acid = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + phospholipid cyclopropane fatty acid.

Name: cysteine sulfinate desulfinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 3-sulfinoalanine = L-alanine + sulfite.

Name: dATP diphosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: dATP + H2O = dAMP + H+ + diphosphate.

Name: dCTP deaminase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: dCTP + H2O = dUTP + NH3.

Name: dTDP-4-dehydrorhamnose 3,5-epimerase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: dTDP-4-dehydro-6-deoxy-alpha-D-glucose = dTDP-4-dehydro-6-deoxy-L-mannose.

Name: dTDP-4-dehydrorhamnose reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: dTDP-6-deoxy-L-mannose + NADP+ = dTDP-4-dehydro-6-deoxy-L-mannose + H+ + NADPH.

Name: dGTPase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: dGTP + H2O = 2'-deoxyguanosine + 2 H+ + triphosphate.

Name: deoxyribonuclease IV (phage-T4-induced) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the endonucleolytic cleavage to 5'-phosphooligonucleotide end-products.

Name: di-trans,poly-cis-undecaprenyl-diphosphate synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: di-trans-poly-cis-decaprenyl diphosphate + isopentenyl diphosphate = diphosphate + di-trans-poly-cis-undecaprenyl diphosphate.

Name: diaminohydroxyphosphoribosylaminopyrimidine deaminase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2,5-diamino-6-hydroxy-4-(5-phosphoribosylamino)-pyrimidine + H2O + H+ = 5-amino-6-(5-phosphoribosylamino)uracil + NH4.

Name: diaminopimelate decarboxylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: meso-2,6-diaminopimelate + H+ = L-lysine + CO2.

Name: diaminopimelate epimerase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: LL-2,6-diaminopimelate = meso-2,6-diaminopimelate.

Name: diaminopropionate ammonia-lyase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2,3-diaminopropionate + H2O = pyruvate + 2 NH3.

Name: 4-hydroxy-tetrahydrodipicolinate reductase
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (S)-2,3,4,5-tetrahydropyridine-2,6-dicarboxylate + NAD(P)+ + H2O = (2S,4S)-4-hydroxy-2,3,4,5-tetrahydrodipicolinate + NAD(P)H + H+.

Name: 4-hydroxy-tetrahydrodipicolinate synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: pyruvate + L-aspartate-4-semialdehyde = (2S,4S)-4-hydroxy-2,3,4,5-tetrahydrodipicolinate + H2O.

Name: dihydrofolate synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + dihydropterate + L-glutamate = ADP + phosphate + dihydrofolate.

Name: diphosphate-purine nucleoside kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: diphosphate + a purine nucleoside = monophosphate + a purine mononucleotide.

Name: endochitinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of nonterminal (1->4)-beta linkages of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (GlcNAc) polymers of chitin and chitodextrins. Typically, endochitinases cleave randomly within the chitin chain.

Name: obsolete endonuclease VIII activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: obsolete endopeptidase La activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the hydrolysis of large proteins such as globin, casein and denatured serum albumin, in presence of ATP.

Name: Enterobacter ribonuclease activity
Definition: Catalysis of the endonucleolytic cleavage to 3'-phosphomononucleotides and 3'-phosphooligonucleotides with 2',3'-cyclic phosphate intermediates.

Name: obsolete enterobactin synthetase
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: enterochelin esterase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: enterobactin + 3 H2O = 3 N-23-dihydroxybenzoyl-L-serine + 3 H+.

Name: ethanolamine ammonia-lyase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ethanolamine = acetaldehyde + NH3.

Name: obsolete exodeoxyribonuclease I activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the degradation of single-stranded DNA. It acts progressively in a 3' to 5' direction, releasing 5'-phosphomononucleotides.

Name: obsolete exodeoxyribonuclease III activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the degradation of double-stranded DNA. It acts progressively in a 3' to 5' direction, releasing 5'-phosphomononucleotides.

Name: exodeoxyribonuclease V activity
Definition: Catalysis of the exonucleolytic cleavage (in the presence of ATP) in either 5' to 3' or 3' to 5' direction to yield 5'-phosphooligonucleotides.

Name: exodeoxyribonuclease VII activity
Definition: Catalysis of the exonucleolytic cleavage in either 5' to 3' or 3' to 5' direction to yield 5'-phosphomononucleotides.

Name: obsolete exodeoxyribonuclease X activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the endonucleolytic cleavage of supercoiled plasma DNA to linear DNA duplexes.

Name: exoribonuclease II activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: RNA + H2O = 5'-phosphomononucleotides. Cleaves RNA in the 3' to 5' direction.

Name: ferredoxin-NAD+ reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: reduced ferredoxin + NAD+ = oxidized ferredoxin + NADH + H+.
column13: "NADH-ferredoxinNAP reductase (component of naphthalene dioxygenase multicomponent enzyme system)"

Name: formate C-acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + formate = CoA + pyruvate.

Name: formate dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: formate + NAD+ = CO2 + NADH.

Name: formyltetrahydrofolate deformylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 10-formyltetrahydrofolate + H2O = (6S)-5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolate + formate + H+.

Name: fructokinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + D-fructose = ADP + D-fructose 6-phosphate.

Name: fructuronate reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-mannonate + NAD+ = D-fructuronate + H+ + NADH.

Name: galactarate dehydratase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: galactarate = 5-dehydro-4-deoxy-D-glucarate + H2O.

Name: galactitol-1-phosphate 5-dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: galactitol-1-phosphate + NAD+ = D-tagatose 6-phosphate + NADH + H+.

Name: galactonate dehydratase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-galactonate = 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-galactonate + H2O.

Name: galactoside O-acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + a beta-D-galactoside = CoA + a 6-acetyl-beta-D-galactoside.

Name: aminoglycoside 2''-nucleotidyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: nucleoside triphosphate + aminoglycoside = diphosphate + 2''-nucleotidylaminoglycoside.

Name: glucarate dehydratase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-glucarate = 5-dehydro-4-deoxy-D-glucarate + H2O.

Name: gluconate 2-dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-gluconate + NADP+ = 2-dehydro-D-gluconate + NADPH + H+.

Name: gluconate 5-dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-gluconate + NADP+ = 5-dehydro-D-gluconate + NADPH + H+.

Name: gluconate dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-gluconate + NADP+ = dehydro-D-gluconate + NADPH + H+.

Name: quinoprotein glucose dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-glucose + ubiquinone = D-glucono-1,5-lactone + ubiquinol.

Name: glucose-1-phosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate + H2O = D-glucose + phosphate.

Name: glucose-1-phosphate adenylyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate + ATP = ADP-glucose + diphosphate.

Name: glucose-1-phosphate thymidylyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate + dTTP = diphosphate + dTDP-glucose.

Name: glucuronate isomerase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-glucuronate = D-fructuronate.

Name: glutamate racemase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-glutamate = D-glutamate.

Name: [glutamate-ammonia-ligase] adenylyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + [L-glutamate:ammonia ligase (ADP-forming)] = diphosphate + adenylyl-[L-glutamate:ammonia ligase (ADP-forming)].

Name: glutamyl-tRNA reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (S)-4-amino-5-oxopentanoate + NADP+ + tRNA(Glu) = L-glutamyl-tRNA(Glu) + H+ + NADPH.

Name: glutathionylspermidine amidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: N1-(gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycyl)-spermidine + H2O = gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycine + spermidine.

Name: glutathionylspermidine synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycine + spermidine + ATP = N1-(gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycyl)-spermidine + ADP + phosphate.
Synonyms: c("gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycine:spermidine ligase (ADP-forming) [spermidine is numbered so that atom N-1 is in the amino group of the aminopropyl part of the molecule]"

Name: glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (NADP+) (non-phosphorylating) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate + H2O + NADP+ = 3-phospho-D-glycerate + 2 H+ + NADPH.

Name: glycerate kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-glycerate + ATP = 3-phospho-D-glycerate + ADP + 2 H+.

Name: glycerol dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: glycerol + NAD+ = glycerone + H+ + NADH.

Name: glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: a glycerophosphodiester + H2O = an alcohol + sn-glycerol 3-phosphate.

Name: glycine C-acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + glycine = L-2-amino-3-oxobutanoate + CoA.

Name: guanine deaminase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: guanine + H2O = xanthine + NH3.

Name: guanosine-3',5'-bis(diphosphate) 3'-diphosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: guanosine 3',5'-bis(diphosphate) + H2O = diphosphate + GDP + H+.

Name: guanosine-5'-triphosphate,3'-diphosphate diphosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: guanosine 5'-triphosphate,3'-diphosphate + H2O = guanosine 5'-diphosphate,3'-diphosphate + phosphate.

Name: holo-[acyl-carrier-protein] synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: CoA + substrate-serine = adenosine 3',5'-bisphosphate + substrate-serine-4'-phosphopantetheine. The transfer of the 4'-phosphopantetheine (Ppant) co-factor from coenzyme A to the hydroxyl side chain of the serine residue of acyl- or peptidyl-carrier protein (ACP or PCP) to convert them from the apo to the holo form.

Name: "CoA:apo-acyl-carrier-protein pantetheinephosphotransferase activity"
Namespace: "coenzyme A:fatty acid synthetase apoenzyme 4'-phosphopantetheine transferase activity"
Definition: "holo-[peptidyl-carrier protein] synthase activity"

Name: "phosphopantetheinyl transferase"
Definition: "PPTase activity")

Name: S-adenosylmethionine-homocysteine S-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + L-homocysteine = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + L-methionine.

Name: homoserine O-succinyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-homoserine + succinyl-CoA = O-succinyl-L-homoserine + CoA.

Name: P-type potassium:proton transporter activity
Definition: Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: ATP + H2O + H+(in) + K+(out) = ADP + phosphate + H+(out) + K+(in).

Name: ferredoxin hydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 reduced ferredoxin + 2 H+ = 2 oxidized ferredoxin + H2.

Name: "nickel hydrogenase activity"
Definition: "nickel-iron-selenium hydrogenase activity"

Name: hydroxymethylpyrimidine kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 4-amino-5-hydroxymethyl-2-methylpyrimidine + ATP = 4-amino-2-methyl-5-phosphomethylpyrimidine + ADP + 2 H+.

Name: hydroxypyruvate isomerase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 3-hydroxypyruvate = 2-hydroxy-3-oxopropanoate.

Name: hygromycin-B 7''-O-phosphotransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + hygromycin B = 7''-O-phosphohygromycin B + ADP + 2 H+.

Name: obsolete mannose-phosphate guanylyltransferase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the transfer of a phosphate group from GTP or GDP to a mannose molecule.

Name: inosine kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + inosine = ADP + IMP.

Name: integrase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the integration of one DNA segment into another.

Name: isochorismatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: H2O + isochorismate = 2,3-dihydroxy-2,3-dihydrobenzoate + pyruvate.

Name: isochorismate synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: chorismate = isochorismate.

Name: kanamycin kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + kanamycin = ADP + 2 H+ + kanamycin 3'-phosphate.

Name: lactaldehyde dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (S)-lactaldehyde + NAD+ + H2O = (S)-lactate + NADH + H+.

Name: lactaldehyde reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: propane-1,2-diol + NAD+ = lactaldehyde + NADH + H+.

Name: lauroyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the transfer of a lauroyl (dodecanoyl) group from one compound to another.

Name: leucyl-tRNA--protein transferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-leucyl-tRNA(Leu) + N-terminal L-arginyl-[protein] = H+ + N-terminal L-leucyl-L-arginyl-[protein] + tRNA(Leu). Can also transfer the leucyl residue on an N-terminal L-lysyl residue.

Name: lipid-A-disaccharide synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2,3-bis(3-hydroxytetradecanoyl)-beta-D-glucosaminyl 1-phosphate + UDP-2,3-bis(3-hydroxytetradecanoyl)-D-glucosamine = 2,3-bis(3-hydroxytetradecanoyl)-D-glucosaminyl-(1->6)-beta-D-2,3-bis(3-hydroxytetradecanoyl)-beta-D-glucosaminyl 1-phosphate + H+ + UDP.

Name: lipopolysaccharide N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: UDP-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine + lipopolysaccharide = UDP + N-acetyl-D-glucosaminyl-lipopolysaccharide.

Name: lipopolysaccharide 3-alpha-galactosyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: UDP-galactose + lipopolysaccharide = UDP + 1,3 alpha-D-galactosyl-lipopolysaccharide.

Name: lipopolysaccharide glucosyltransferase I activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: UDP-glucose + lipopolysaccharide = UDP + D-glucosyl-lipopolysaccharide.

Name: lipopolysaccharide heptosyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: a lipopolysaccharide + ADP-L-glycero-beta-D-manno-heptose = a heptosylated lipopolysaccharide + ADP + H+.

Name: lipopolysaccharide-1,6-galactosyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: UDP-galactose + lipopolysaccharide = UDP + 1,6 alpha-D-galactosyl-lipopolysaccharide.

Name: long-chain fatty acid [acyl-carrier-protein] ligase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: a long-chain fatty acid + ATP + holo-[ACP] = a long-chain fatty acyl-[ACP] + AMP + diphosphate. A long-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 13 to 22 carbons.

Name: lysine decarboxylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-lysine + H+ = cadaverine + CO2.

Name: L-malate dehydrogenase (quinone) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (S)-malate + a quinone = oxaloacetate + a quinol. Vitamin K (menaquinone) and several other quinones can act as acceptors.

Name: maltose O-acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + maltose = CoA + acetyl-maltose.

Name: mannitol-1-phosphate 5-dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-mannitol 1-phosphate + NAD+ = D-fructose 6-phosphate + NADH + H+.

Name: mannonate dehydratase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-mannonate = 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-gluconate + H2O.

Name: mannose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase (GDP) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: alpha-D-mannose 1-phosphate + GDP + H+ = GDP-alpha-D-mannose + phosphate.

Name: methylglyoxal synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: glycerone phosphate = methylglyoxal + phosphate.

Name: methylthioadenosine nucleosidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: methylthioadenosine + H2O = adenine + 5-methylthio-D-ribose.

Name: obsolete murein DD-endopeptidase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: lytic endotransglycosylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the specific cleavage of the beta-(1->4) glycosidic linkage between N-acetylmuramyl and N-acetylglucosaminyl residues in peptidoglycan, with the concomitant formation of 1,6-anhydro-N-acetylmuramyl residues. Acts on linkages within peptidoglycan chains (i.e. not at the ends) to produce shorter strands with 1,6-anhydromuramic acid ends.

Name: lytic transglycosylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the specific cleavage of the beta-(1->4) glycosidic linkage between N-acetylmuramyl and N-acetylglucosaminyl residues in peptidoglycan, with the concomitant formation of 1,6-anhydro-N-acetylmuramyl residues.

Name: inositol monophosphate 1-phosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: myo-inositol 1-phosphate + H2O = myo-inositol + phosphate.

Name: 1,4-dihydroxy-2-naphthoyl-CoA synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2-succinylbenzoyl-CoA + H+ = 1,4-dihydroxy-2-naphthoyl-CoA + H2O.

Name: nicotinamidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: nicotinamide + H2O = nicotinate + NH3.

Name: ferredoxin-NAD(P) reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: reduced ferredoxin + NAD(P)+ = oxidized ferredoxin + NAD(P)H + H+.

Name: nicotinate N-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine(1+) + nicotinate = N-methylnicotinate + S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine.

Name: nicotinate-nucleotide-dimethylbenzimidazole phosphoribosyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole + nicotinate D-ribonucleotide = alpha-ribazole 5'-phosphate + H+ + nicotinate.

Name: nitrate reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: nitrite + acceptor = nitrate + reduced acceptor.

Name: nitric oxide dioxygenase NAD(P)H activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 NO + 2 O2 + NAD(P)H + H+ = 2 nitrate + NAD(P)+.

Name: nitrite reductase [NAD(P)H] activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: NH4+ + 3 NAD(P)+ + 2 H2O = nitrite + 3 NAD(P)H + 5 H+.

Name: obsolete glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reactions: glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate + phosphate + NAD(P)+ = 3-phospho-D-glyceroyl-phosphate + NAD(P)H + H+, and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate + H2O + NAD(P)+ = 3-phospho-D-glycerate + NAD(P)H + H+.

Name: obsolete oligopeptidase A activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the hydrolysis of oligopeptides, with broad specificity. Gly or Ala commonly occur as P1 or P1' residues, but more distant residues are also important, as is shown by the fact that Z-Gly-Pro-Gly-Gly-Pro-Ala is cleaved at the Gly-Gly bond, but not Z-(Gly)5.

Name: obsolete oligopeptidase B activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the hydrolysis of Arg-Xaa and Lys-Xaa bonds in oligopeptides, even when P1' residue is proline.

Name: oligonucleotidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the exonucleolytic cleavage of oligonucleotides to yield nucleoside 5'-phosphates.

Name: obsolete omptin activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the preferential cleavage of Xaa-Yaa in which both Xaa and Yaa are Arg or Lys.

Name: oxaloacetate decarboxylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: oxaloacetate = pyruvate + CO2.

Name: oxalyl-CoA decarboxylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: H+ + oxalyl-CoA = CO2 + formyl-CoA.

Name: obsolete p-aminobenzoate synthetase
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: palmitoleoyl [acyl-carrier-protein]-dependent acyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: a palmitoleoyl-[acyl-carrier protein] + alpha-KDO-(2->4)-alpha-KDO-(2->6)-lipid IVA = KDO2-(palmitoleoyl)-lipid IVA + a holo-[acyl-carrier protein].

Name: penicillin amidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: penicillin + H2O = a carboxylate + 6-aminopenicillanate.

Name: obsolete peptidoglycan synthetase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: [GlcNAc-(1->4)-Mur2Ac(oyl-L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu-L-Lys-D-Ala-D-Ala)](n)-di-trans,octa-cis-undecaprenyl diphosphate + beta-D-GlcNAc-(1->4)-Mur2Ac(oyl-L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu-L-Lys-D-Ala-D-Ala)-di-trans,octa-cis-undecaprenyl diphosphate = [GlcNAc-(1->4)-Mur2Ac(oyl-L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu-L-Lys-D-Ala-D-Ala)](n+1)-di-trans-octa-cis-undecaprenyl diphosphate + di-trans,octa-cis-undecaprenyl diphosphate + H+.

Name: obsolete peptidyl-dipeptidase Dcp activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the hydrolysis of unblocked, C-terminal dipeptides from oligopeptides, with broad specificity. Does not hydrolyze bonds in which P1' is Pro, or both P1 and P1' are Gly.

Name: phenylacetaldehyde dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2-phenylacetaldehyde + H2O + NAD+ = 2-phenylacetate + 2 H+ + NADH.

Name: phosphate acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + phosphate = CoA + acetyl phosphate.

Name: phosphatidylglycerol-membrane-oligosaccharide glycerophosphotransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: phosphatidylglycerol + membrane-derived-oligosaccharide D-glucose = 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol + membrane-derived-oligosaccharide 6-(glycerophospho)-D-glucose.

Name: phosphatidylglycerol-prolipoprotein diacylglyceryl transferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the transfer of the diacylglyceryl group from phosphatidylglycerol to the sulfhydryl group of the prospective N-terminal cysteine residue in an unmodified prolipoprotein.

Name: phosphatidylglycerophosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: phosphatidylglycerophosphate + H2O = phosphatidylglycerol + phosphate.

Name: phospho-N-acetylmuramoyl-pentapeptide-transferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamyl-L-lysyl-D-alanyl-D-alanine + undecaprenyl phosphate = UMP + N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamyl-L-lysyl-D-alanyl-D-alanine-diphosphoundecaprenol.

Name: "UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala-D-gamma-Glu-L-Lys-D-Ala-D-Ala:C(55)-isoprenoid alcohol transferase activity"
Definition: "UDP-MurNAc-pentapeptide phosphotransferase activity")

Name: phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: phosphate + oxaloacetate = phosphoenolpyruvate + HCO3-.

Name: phosphoenolpyruvate-protein phosphotransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: phosphoenolpyruvate + protein L-histidine = pyruvate + protein N(pi)-phospho-L-histidine.
Synonyms: c("enzyme I of the phosphotransferase system"

Name: phosphoglucosamine mutase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: alpha-D-glucosamine 1-phosphate = D-glucosamine 6-phosphate.

Name: phosphoglycolate phosphatase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2-phosphoglycolate + H2O = glycolate + phosphate.

Name: D-sedoheptulose 7-phosphate isomerase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate = D-alpha,beta-D-heptose 7-phosphate.

Name: phospholipase A1 activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: phosphatidylcholine + H2O = 2-acylglycerophosphocholine + a carboxylate.

Name: phosphomethylpyrimidine kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + 4-amino-2-methyl-5-phosphomethylpyrimidine = ADP + 4-amino-2-methyl-5-diphosphomethylpyrimidine.

Name: phosphopentomutase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-ribose 1-phosphate = D-ribose 5-phosphate.

Name: phosphoribulokinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-ribulose 5-phosphate + ATP = D-ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate + ADP + 2 H+.

Name: obsolete pitrilysin activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the preferential cleavage of Tyr16-Leu17 and Phe25-Tyr26 bonds of oxidized insulin B chain. Also acts on other substrates of Molecular weight less than 7 kDa such as insulin and glucagon.

Name: polyphosphate kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + phosphate(n) = ADP + phosphate(n+1).

Name: prephenate dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: NAD+ + prephenate = (4-hydroxyphenyl)pyruvate + CO2 + NADH.

Name: obsolete prepilin peptidase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the cleavage of a Gly-Phe bond to release an N-terminal, basic peptide of 5-8 residues from type IV prepilin, and then N-methylates the new N-terminal amino group, the methyl donor being S-adenosyl-L-methionine.

Name: prophage integrase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the integration of prophage DNA into a target DNA molecule, usually a bacterial chromosome, via a sequence-specific recombination event which involves the formation of an intasome, a DNA-protein-complex designed for site-specific recombination of the phage and host DNA.
Synonyms: integrase activity involved in establishment of integrated proviral latency

Name: propionate kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + propanoate = ADP + propanoyl phosphate.

Name: obsolete protease IV activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: protein-N(PI)-phosphohistidine-sugar phosphotransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the PEP-dependent, phosphoryl transfer-driven transport of substances across a membrane. The transport happens by catalysis of the reaction: protein N-phosphohistidine + sugar(out) = protein histidine + sugar phosphate(in). This differs from primary and secondary active transport in that the solute is modified during transport.
Synonyms: c("enzyme II of the phosphotransferase system"

Name: protein-glutamate O-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + protein L-glutamate = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + protein L-glutamate 5-methyl ester; this reaction is the methylation of peptidyl-L-glutamate to form peptidyl-L-glutamate 5-methyl ester.

Name: "protein(aspartate)methyltransferase activity"
Definition: "S-adenosyl-L-methionine:protein-L-glutamate O-methyltransferase activity"

Name: protein-glutamate methylesterase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: protein L-glutamate O(5)-methyl ester + H2O = protein L-glutamate + methanol.

Name: obsolete pyruvate dehydrogenase (cytochrome) activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: pyruvate + ferricytochrome b1 + H2O = CO2 + acetate + ferrocytochrome b1.

Name: pyruvate, water dikinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + H2O + pyruvate = AMP + 3 H+ + phosphate + phosphoenolpyruvate.

Name: quinolinate synthetase A activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: iminoaspartate + dihydroxy-acetone-phosphate = quinolinate + 2 H2O + phosphate.

Name: rRNA (adenine-N6-)-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + rRNA = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + rRNA containing N6-methyladenine.

Name: rRNA (guanine-N1-)-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + rRNA = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + rRNA containing N1-methylguanine.

Name: rRNA (guanine-N2-)-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + rRNA = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + rRNA containing N2-methylguanine.

Name: obsolete serine-type signal peptidase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the cleavage of a signal peptide from a protein precursor by a serine endopeptidase mechanism.

Name: obsolete repressor LexA activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the hydrolysis of Ala-Gly bond in repressor lexA.

Name: rhamnulokinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + L-rhamnulose = ADP + L-rhamnulose 1-phosphate.

Name: rhamnulose-1-phosphate aldolase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-rhamnulose 1-phosphate = glycerone phosphate + (S)-lactaldehyde.

Name: ribonuclease E activity
Definition: Catalysis of the cleavage of single-stranded RNA that is monophosphorylated at its 5'-end; cleavage occurs predominantly at 5 nucleotides from the 5'-end and in A + U-rich regions, and is blocked by the presence of a 5'-triphosphate group.

Name: ribonuclease G activity
Definition: Catalysis of the cleavage of single-stranded RNA that is monophosphorylated at its 5'-end; cleavage occurs predominantly at positions 5 and 6 nucleotides from the 5'-end and in A + U-rich regions, and is blocked by the presence of a 5'-triphosphate group.

Name: ribonuclease R activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: RNA + H2O = 5'-phosphomononucleotides. Cleaves RNA in the 3' to 5' direction, leaving an undigested core of 3-5 nucleotides.

Name: ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (thioredoxin) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: [thioredoxin]-disulfide + a 2'-deoxyribonucleoside 5'-triphosphate + H2O = [thioredoxin]-dithiol + a ribonucleoside 5'-triphosphate.

Name: peptide-alanine-alpha-N-acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: acetyl-CoA + N-terminal L-alanyl-peptide = CoA + H+ + N-terminal N-alpha-acetyl-L-alanyl-peptide.

Name: selenocysteine lyase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-selenocysteine + reduced acceptor = hydrogen selenide + L-alanine + acceptor.

Name: serine O-acetyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-serine + acetyl-CoA = O-acetyl-L-serine + CoA.

Name: serine-type D-Ala-D-Ala carboxypeptidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (Ac)2-L-Lys-D-alanyl-D-alanine + H2O = (Ac)2-L-Lys-D-alanine + D-alanine.

Name: obsolete signal peptidase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the cleavage of a signal peptide from a protein precursor.

Name: obsolete signal peptidase I activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the cleavage of N-terminal leader sequences from secreted and periplasmic proteins precursor.

Name: "signal peptide hydrolase activity"
Definition: "signalase activity"

Name: obsolete signal peptidase II activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the cleavage of N-terminal leader sequences from membrane prolipoproteins. Hydrolyzes the terminal bond of Xaa-Xbb-Xbb-Cys, in which Xaa is hydrophobic (preferably Leu), Xbb is often Ser or Ala, Xcc is often Gly or Ala, and the Cys is alkylated on sulfur with a diacylglyceryl group.

Name: obsolete siroheme synthase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

Name: site-specific DNA-methyltransferase (adenine-specific) activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + DNA adenine = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + DNA 6-methylaminopurine.

Name: DNA-methyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the transfer of a methyl group to a DNA molecule.

Name: site-specific recombinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the formation of new phosphodiester bonds between a pair of short, unique target DNA sequences.

Name: sorbitol-6-phosphate 2-dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-sorbitol 6-phosphate + NAD+ = D-fructose 6-phosphate + NADH + H+.

Name: starch synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ADP-glucose + (1,4)-alpha-D-glucosyl(n) = ADP + (1,4)-alpha-D-glucosyl(n+1).

Name: aminoglycoside 3''-adenylyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + streptomycin = 3''-adenylylstreptomycin + diphosphate + H+.

Name: succinate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase [NAD(P)+] activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: succinate semialdehyde + NAD(P)+ + H2O = succinate + NAD(P)H + H+.

Name: succinyl-diaminopimelate desuccinylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: N-succinyl-LL-2,6-diaminopimelate + H2O = LL-2,6-diaminopimelate + succinate.

Name: N-succinylarginine dihydrolase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: N(2)-succinyl-L-arginine + 2 H2O + 2 H+ = N(2)-succinyl-L-ornithine + CO2 + 2 NH4.

Name: succinyldiaminopimelate transaminase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2-oxoglutarate + N-succinyl-LL-2,6-diaminopimelate = L-2-succinylamino-6-oxopimelate + L-glutamate.

Name: succinylglutamate desuccinylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: N-succinyl-L-glutamate + H2O = L-glutamate + succinate.

Name: sucrose phosphorylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: sucrose + phosphate = D-fructose + alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate.

Name: obsolete tRNA (guanine-N1-)-methyltransferase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + tRNA = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + tRNA containing N1-methylguanine.

Name: obsolete tRNA (guanosine-2'-O-)-methyltransferase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + tRNA = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + tRNA containing 2'-O-methylguanosine.

Name: tRNA nucleotidyltransferase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: tRNA(n+1) + phosphate = tRNA(n) + a nucleoside diphosphate.

Name: obsolete tRNA sulfurtransferase
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: L-cysteine + activated-tRNA = L-serine + tRNA containing a thionucleotide.

Name: tagatose-6-phosphate kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + D-tagatose 6-phosphate = ADP + D-tagatose 1,6-bisphosphate.

Name: tagatose-bisphosphate aldolase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-tagatose 1,6-diphosphate = D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate + glycerone phosphate.

Name: tagaturonate reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-altronate + NAD+ = D-tagaturonate + H+ + NADH.

Name: tartrate dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: tartrate + NAD+ = oxaloglycolate + NADH + H+.

Name: tartronate-semialdehyde synthase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 glyoxylate + H+ = 2-hydroxy-3-oxopropanoate + CO2.

Name: tetraacyldisaccharide 4'-kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2,3-bis(3-hydroxytetradecanoyl)-D-glucosaminyl-(1->6)-beta-D-2,3-bis(3-hydroxytetradecanoyl)-beta-D-glucosaminyl 1-phosphate + ATP = ADP + 2 H+ + lipid IV(a).

Name: thiamine-phosphate kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + thiamine phosphate = ADP + H+ + thiamine diphosphate.

Name: thymidine phosphorylase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: thymidine + phosphate = thymine + 2-deoxy-D-ribose 1-phosphate.

Name: trimethylamine-N-oxide reductase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: NADH + H+ + trimethylamine-N-oxide = NAD+ + trimethylamine + H2O.

Name: tryptophanase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-tryptophan + H2O = indole + NH4 + pyruvate.

Name: type I site-specific deoxyribonuclease activity
Definition: Catalysis of the endonucleolytic cleavage of DNA to give random double-stranded fragments with terminal 5' or 3' protrusions, driven by ATP hydrolysis. Cleavage is dependent on the presence in the DNA of a specific recognition site. Cleavage may occur hundreds or thousands of base pairs away from the recognition site due to translocation of DNA.

Name: type II site-specific deoxyribonuclease activity
Definition: Catalysis of the endonucleolytic cleavage of DNA to give specific double-stranded fragments with terminal 5'-phosphates and 3' hydroxyls. Cleavage is dependent on the presence in the DNA of a specific recognition site; cleavage occurs at or very near this recognition site.

Name: tyrosine-based site-specific recombinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the formation of new phosphodiester bonds between a pair of short, unique DNA target sequences; occurs through a phosphotyrosyl intermediate in which the target sequence is first cleaved by the nucleophilic attack by a tyrosine in the active site.

Name: undecaprenol kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + undecaprenol = ADP + undecaprenyl phosphate.

Name: urease activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: urea + H2O = CO2 + 2 NH3.

Name: ureidoglycolate dehydrogenase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: (S)-ureidoglycolate + NAD(P)+ = oxalureate + NAD(P)H + H+.

Name: UMP/dUMP kinase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + (d)UMP = ADP + (d)UDP.

Name: valine-pyruvate transaminase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-valine + pyruvate = 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate + L-alanine.

Name: xylan 1,4-beta-xylosidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of (1->4)-beta-D-xylans so as to remove successive D-xylose residues from the non-reducing termini.

Name: xylose isomerase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the reaction: D-xylose = D-xylulose.

Name: zinc D-Ala-D-Ala carboxypeptidase activity
Definition: Catalysis of the cleavage of the D-alanyl-D-alanine bond in (Ac)2-L-lysyl-D-alanyl-D-alanine.

Name: dosage compensation by hyperactivation of X chromosome
Definition: Compensating for the two-fold variation in X-chromosome:autosome ratios between sexes by a global hyperactivation of all, or most of, the genes on the X-chromosome in the heterogametic sex, leading to a two-fold increase in gene expression from this chromosome. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

Name: dosage compensation by inactivation of X chromosome
Definition: Compensating for the two-fold variation in X-chromosome:autosome ratios between sexes by heterochromatin formation leading to a global inactivation of all, or most of, the genes on one of the X-chromosomes in the XX sex.

Name: obsolete aspartic-type signal peptidase activity
Definition: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the cleavage of a signal peptide from a protein precursor by an aspartic endopeptidase mechanism.

Name: glycopeptide catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of glycopeptides, a compound in which carbohydrate is covalently attached to an oligopeptide composed of residues of L and/or D-amino acids. The term usually denotes a product of proteolytic degradation of a glycoprotein but includes glycated peptide.

Name: pentose-phosphate shunt, oxidative branch
Definition: The branch of the pentose-phosphate shunt which involves the oxidation of glucose 6-P and produces ribulose 5-P, reduced NADP+ and carbon dioxide (CO2).

Name: pentose-phosphate shunt, non-oxidative branch
Definition: The branch of the pentose-phosphate shunt which does not involve oxidation reactions. It comprises a series of sugar phosphate interconversions, starting with ribulose 5-P and producing fructose 6-P and glyceraldehyde 3-P.

Name: electron transfer activity
Definition: A molecular function representing the directed movement of electrons from one molecular entity to another, typically mediated by electron carriers or acceptors, resulting in the transfer of energy and/or the reduction-oxidation (redox) transformation of chemical species. This activity is fundamental to various biological processes, including cellular respiration and photosynthesis, as well as numerous enzymatic reactions involved in metabolic pathways.

Name: catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances, including the breakdown of carbon compounds with the liberation of energy for use by the cell or organism.

Name: macromolecule catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

Name: biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of substances; typically the energy-requiring part of metabolism in which simpler substances are transformed into more complex ones.

Name: macromolecule biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

Name: aerobic respiration
Definition: The enzymatic release of energy from inorganic and organic compounds (especially carbohydrates and fats) which requires oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor.

Name: anaerobic respiration
Definition: The enzymatic release of energy from inorganic and organic compounds (especially carbohydrates and fats) which uses compounds other than oxygen (e.g. nitrate, sulfate) as the terminal electron acceptor.

Name: fatty acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a fatty acid, any of the aliphatic monocarboxylic acids that can be liberated by hydrolysis from naturally occurring fats and oils. Fatty acids are predominantly straight-chain acids of 4 to 24 carbon atoms, which may be saturated or unsaturated; branched fatty acids and hydroxy fatty acids also occur, and very long chain acids of over 30 carbons are found in waxes.

Name: amino acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids, organic acids containing one or more amino substituents.

Name: glutamine family amino acid metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.

Name: glutamine family amino acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.

Name: aspartate family amino acid metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the aspartate family, comprising asparagine, aspartate, lysine, methionine and threonine.

Name: aspartate family amino acid biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids of the aspartate family, comprising asparagine, aspartate, lysine, methionine and threonine.

Name: aspartate family amino acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids of the aspartate family, comprising asparagine, aspartate, lysine, methionine and threonine.

Name: serine family amino acid metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

Name: serine family amino acid biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

Name: serine family amino acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

Name: aromatic amino acid metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).
Synonyms: c("aromatic amino acid family metabolic process"

Name: aromatic amino acid family biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).

Name: aromatic amino acid family catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).

Name: obsolete histidine family amino acid metabolic process
Definition: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the histidine family.
Synonyms: c("histidine family amino acid metabolic process"

Name: obsolete histidine family amino acid biosynthetic process
Definition: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids of the histidine family.

Name: obsolete histidine family amino acid catabolic process
Definition: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids of the histidine family.

Name: pyruvate family amino acid metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any amino acid that requires pyruvate for its synthesis, e.g. alanine.

Name: pyruvate family amino acid biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of any amino acid that requires pyruvate for its synthesis, e.g. alanine.

Name: pyruvate family amino acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of any amino acid that requires pyruvate for its synthesis, e.g. alanine.

Name: branched-chain amino acid metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.
Synonyms: branched chain family amino acid metabolism

Name: branched-chain amino acid biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.
Synonyms: c("branched chain family amino acid anabolism"
column7: "branched chain family amino acid biosynthetic process"

Name: branched-chain amino acid catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.
Synonyms: c("branched chain family amino acid breakdown"
Is_a: "branched chain family amino acid catabolic process"

Name: glutamine family amino acid biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.

Name: lysine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lysine, 2,6-diaminohexanoic acid.

Name: methionine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of methionine (2-amino-4-(methylthio)butanoic acid), a sulfur-containing, essential amino acid found in peptide linkage in proteins.

Name: methionine catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of methionine (2-amino-4-(methylthio)butanoic acid), a sulfur-containing, essential amino acid found in peptide linkage in proteins.

Name: threonine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of threonine (2-amino-3-hydroxybutyric acid), a polar, uncharged, essential amino acid found in peptide linkage in proteins.

Name: lysine biosynthetic process via diaminopimelate
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lysine, via the intermediate diaminopimelate.

Name: homoserine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of homoserine, alpha-amino-gamma-hydroxybutyric acid.

Name: homoserine catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of homoserine, alpha-amino-gamma-hydroxybutyric acid.

Name: homoserine metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving homoserine, alpha-amino-gamma-hydroxybutyric acid, an intermediate in the biosynthesis of cystathionine, threonine and methionine.

Name: cysteine catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of cysteine, 2-amino-3-mercaptopropanoic acid.

Name: L-phenylalanine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of L-phenylalanine, the L-enantiomer of 2-amino-3-phenylpropanoic acid, i.e. (2S)-2-amino-3-phenylpropanoic acid.

Name: aromatic amino acid family biosynthetic process, prephenate pathway
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phenylalanine and tyrosine from other compounds, including chorismate, via the intermediate prephenate.

column8: "aromatic amino acid family biosynthetic process via prephenate(2-)"

Name: isoleucine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of isoleucine, (2R*,3R*)-2-amino-3-methylpentanoic acid.

Name: L-leucine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of L-leucine, 2-amino-4-methylpentanoic acid.

Name: valine biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of valine, 2-amino-3-methylbutanoic acid.

Name: glycoprotein metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

Name: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

Name: biotin biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of biotin, cis-tetrahydro-2-oxothieno(3,4-d)imidazoline-4-valeric acid.

Name: lipopolysaccharide biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipopolysaccharides, any of a group of related, structurally complex components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria.

Name: lipopolysaccharide catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lipopolysaccharides, any of a group of related, structurally complex components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria.

Name: lipoate metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving lipoate, 1,2-dithiolane-3-pentanoate, the anion derived from lipoic acid.

Name: lipoate biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipoate, 1,2-dithiolane-3-pentanoate, the anion derived from lipoic acid.

Name: obsolete coenzyme biosynthetic process
Definition: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of coenzymes, any of various nonprotein organic cofactors that are required, in addition to an enzyme and a substrate, for an enzymatic reaction to proceed.

Name: obsolete coenzyme catabolic process
Definition: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of coenzymes, any of various nonprotein organic cofactors that are required, in addition to an enzyme and a substrate, for an enzymatic reaction to proceed.
Synonyms: c("coenzyme and prosthetic group catabolic process"

Name: vitamin biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a vitamin, one of a number of unrelated organic substances that occur in many foods in small amounts and that are necessary in trace amounts for the normal metabolic functioning of the body.

Name: vitamin catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a vitamin, one of a number of unrelated organic substances that occur in many foods in small amounts and that are necessary in trace amounts for the normal metabolic functioning of the body.

Name: nucleobase metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleobase, a nitrogenous base that is a constituent of a nucleic acid, e.g. the purines: adenine, guanine, hypoxanthine, xanthine and the pyrimidines: cytosine, uracil, thymine.

Name: purine nucleobase biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine nucleobases, one of the two classes of nitrogen-containing ring compounds found in DNA and RNA, which include adenine and guanine.

Name: hypoxanthine catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of hypoxanthine, 6-hydroxy purine, an intermediate in the degradation of adenylate. Its ribonucleoside is known as inosine and its ribonucleotide as inosinate.

Name: xanthine catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of xanthine, 2,6-dihydroxypurine, a purine formed in the metabolic breakdown of guanine but not present in nucleic acids.

Name: nucleoside metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside, a nucleobase linked to either beta-D-ribofuranose (a ribonucleoside) or 2-deoxy-beta-D-ribofuranose, (a deoxyribonucleoside), e.g. adenosine, guanosine, inosine, cytidine, uridine and deoxyadenosine, deoxyguanosine, deoxycytidine and thymidine (= deoxythymidine).

Name: nucleotide metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleotide, a nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the glycose moiety; may be mono-, di- or triphosphate; this definition includes cyclic nucleotides (nucleoside cyclic phosphates).

Name: regulation of nucleoside metabolic process
Definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving nucleosides.

Name: ribonucleoside metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any ribonucleoside, a nucleoside in which purine or pyrimidine base is linked to a ribose (beta-D-ribofuranose) molecule.

Name: deoxyribonucleoside metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any one of a family of organic molecules consisting of a purine or pyrimidine base covalently bonded to a sugar deoxyribose (a deoxyribonucleoside).

Name: nucleoside monophosphate metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: nucleoside monophosphate biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: nucleoside monophosphate catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: purine nucleoside monophosphate metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving purine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: purine nucleoside monophosphate biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: purine nucleoside monophosphate catabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of purine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphate metabolic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a pyrimidine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphate biosynthetic process
Definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphate, a compound consisting of a pyrimidine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with phosphate on the sugar.

Name: pyrimidine nucleoside monophosphate catabolic process
